records.source: Παῦλος δοῦλος θεοῦ, ἀπόστολος δὲ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ κατὰ πίστιν ἐκλεκτῶν θεοῦ καὶ ἐπίγνωσιν ἀληθείας τῆς κατ’ εὐσέβειαν ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι ζωῆς αἰωνίου, ἣν ἐπηγγείλατο ὁ ἀψευδὴς θεὸς πρὸ χρόνων αἰωνίων ἐφανέρωσεν δὲ καιροῖς ἰδίοις, τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ ἐν κηρύγματι ὃ ἐπιστεύθην ἐγὼ κατ’ ἐπιταγὴν τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν θεοῦ, Τίτῳ γνησίῳ τέκνῳ κατὰ κοινὴν πίστιν· χάρις καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς καὶ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν.
records.gloss: Paul, slave of God, apostle and of Jesus Christ for [the] faith of [the] chosen of God and knowledge of truth the [one] according to godliness, \v 2 in hope of life eternal, which promised the not-lying God before times eternal, \v 3 revealed but in times his own the word of him in [the] proclamation with which was entrusted I according to [the] command of the Savior of us God, \v 4 to Titus true child according to common faith: grace and peace from God Father and Christ Jesus the Savior of us.
pieces: From Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. I was sent to bring God's chosen people to faith and to the knowledge of the truth that leads to godliness,
a faith and knowledge resting on the hope of eternal life. God, who never lies, promised this life before eternal ages began,
and at the right time {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word known through the preaching entrusted to me by the command of God our Savior.
To Titus, my true son in the faith we share: grace and peace from God the Father and {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus our Savior.

L.1: Paul, a slave of God and an apostle of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, for the faith of God's chosen ones and the knowledge of the truth that accords with godliness,
L.2: in hope of eternal life, which God, who does not lie, promised before eternal ages,
L.3: and at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own proper time revealed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word in the proclamation with which I was entrusted by the command of God our Savior,
L.4: to Titus, [my] true child in a common faith: grace and peace from God [the] Father and {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus our Savior.

R.1: This letter is from Paul. I am a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. God sent me to help the people {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has chosen to have faith in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and to know the truth that teaches them how to live for God.
R.2: This faith and truth give us hope of eternal life. Before the eternal ages began, God promised to give this life, and God never lies.
R.3: Now, at the right time, God has made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} message known. He gave me the work of telling it, because God our Savior commanded me to.
R.4: I am writing to Titus. You are like a true son to me, because we share the same faith. I pray that God the Father and {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus our Savior will show you grace and give you peace.

decisions.reason: δοῦλος is a slave. Only here does Paul call himself a slave "of God" rather than "of Christ"; the phrase recalls Moses and the prophets.

decisions.choice: for the faith of God's chosen: the purpose of his apostleship
alternatives: in keeping with the faith of God's chosen
decisions.reason: κατὰ may give the purpose (to bring the chosen to faith and knowledge) or the standard (an apostle in line with their faith). Most take it as purpose.
ἀψευδὴς is "free of falsehood". It sets God against the Cretans, "always liars" (1:12).

decisions.choice: before eternal ages: before time began
decisions.reason: As in 2 Timothy 1:9.

A Greek believer and Paul's co-worker (Galatians 2:1-3; 2 Corinthians 8:23). Paul had left him in Crete (verse 5). As with the letters to Timothy, the letter's authorship has been questioned since the nineteenth century; it presents itself as Paul's.

decisions.choice: God our Savior ... Christ Jesus our Savior
decisions.reason: The letter calls both God and Christ "our Savior", side by side (also 2:10, 2:13, 3:4, 3:6).
"Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".
ἐπιστεύθην is the passive of the verb "believe", which here means to be entrusted with something (as in 1 Timothy 1:11).

decisions.choice: entrusted (L, B); gave me the work (R)
decisions.reason: The sense is entrusting (m7), so the key term "believe" is not used for this word.
Title setting.
As in 1 Timothy 1:2.

decisions.choice: I was sent to bring (B); God sent me to help (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the sense chosen in m2.

records.source: Τούτου χάριν ἀπέλιπόν σε ἐν Κρήτῃ ἵνα τὰ λείποντα ἐπιδιορθώσῃ, καὶ καταστήσῃς κατὰ πόλιν πρεσβυτέρους, ὡς ἐγώ σοι διεταξάμην, εἴ τίς ἐστιν ἀνέγκλητος, μιᾶς γυναικὸς ἀνήρ, τέκνα ἔχων πιστά, μὴ ἐν κατηγορίᾳ ἀσωτίας ἢ ἀνυπότακτα.
records.gloss: For this reason I left you in Crete, so that the things lacking you might set in order and appoint in every city elders, as I you directed, \v 6 if anyone is blameless, of one wife husband, children having believing, not under accusation of debauchery or insubordinate.
pieces: I left you in Crete so that you could put in order what was left unfinished and appoint elders in every town, as I told you to.
An elder must be blameless, the husband of one wife, with children who believe and are not open to the charge of wild living or disobedience.

L.5: For this reason I left you in Crete, so that you might set in order what remains and appoint elders in every town as I directed you:
L.6: if anyone is blameless, the husband of one wife, having children who believe, not accused of debauchery or insubordination.

R.5: I left you on the island of Crete so that you could finish the work that still needed to be done. I also told you to choose leaders for the church in every town.
R.6: A leader must be someone people cannot find fault with. He must be faithful to his wife. His children must be believers, and people must not be able to say that they are wild or will not obey.

decisions.reason: A large island south of Greece. Acts does not tell of Paul founding churches there; he passed it as a prisoner on the way to Rome (Acts 27:7-13).
πρεσβυτέρους is "older men", the title of the leaders of a congregation (Acts 14:23). Verse 7 calls the same office "overseer".

Literally "a one-woman man", as in 1 Timothy 3:2. It may require faithfulness in marriage, rule out polygamy, or rule out remarriage. Most now take it as marital faithfulness; the phrase does not settle whether an elder must be married.
πιστά can mean "believing" or "faithful". With "not accused of wild living" it may describe behavior rather than faith.
Readable follows the sense most now take (m3).
Readable explains the title (m2).

records.source: δεῖ γὰρ τὸν ἐπίσκοπον ἀνέγκλητον εἶναι ὡς θεοῦ οἰκονόμον, μὴ αὐθάδη, μὴ ὀργίλον, μὴ πάροινον, μὴ πλήκτην, μὴ αἰσχροκερδῆ, ἀλλὰ φιλόξενον, φιλάγαθον, σώφρονα, δίκαιον, ὅσιον, ἐγκρατῆ, ἀντεχόμενον τοῦ κατὰ τὴν διδαχὴν πιστοῦ λόγου, ἵνα δυνατὸς ᾖ καὶ παρακαλεῖν ἐν τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ τῇ ὑγιαινούσῃ καὶ τοὺς ἀντιλέγοντας ἐλέγχειν.
records.gloss: It is necessary for the overseer blameless to be as God's steward, not arrogant, not quick-tempered, not given to wine, not violent, not greedy for gain, \v 8 but hospitable, lover of good, self-controlled, just, holy, disciplined, \v 9 holding to the according to the teaching faithful word, so that able he may be both to exhort in the teaching the sound and those contradicting to reprove.
pieces: Since an overseer manages God's household, he must be blameless. He must not be arrogant or quick-tempered, not a drunkard or violent, not greedy for money.
He must be hospitable, love what is good, and be self-controlled, upright, holy and disciplined.
He must hold firmly to the trustworthy message as it has been taught, so that he can encourage others with sound teaching and correct those who oppose it.

L.7: For the overseer must be blameless as God's steward, not arrogant, not quick-tempered, not a drunkard, not violent, not greedy for gain,
L.8: but hospitable, a lover of good, self-controlled, just, holy, disciplined,
L.9: holding firmly to the trustworthy word as taught, so that he may be able both to exhort with sound teaching and to rebuke those who contradict [it].

R.7: A church leader takes care of God's family, so people must not be able to find fault with him. He must not be proud or get angry quickly. He must not drink too much wine or like to fight. He must not try to get money in dishonest ways.
R.8: He must welcome guests into his home and love what is good. He must control himself and do what is right. He must be holy and disciplined.
R.9: He must hold on to the true message we teach, so that he can encourage people with true teaching and show those who are against it that they are wrong.

decisions.choice: the overseer: the same office as the elders
decisions.reason: ἐπίσκοπον is one who watches over; "bishop" comes from it. Verse 5 calls the same leaders "elders".

decisions.choice: God's steward: the manager of God's household
decisions.reason: οἰκονόμον is a household manager, often a slave, entrusted with the master's goods (Luke 12:42). The church is God's household (1 Timothy 3:15).
πάροινον is one who sits long at wine; πλήκτην is one who strikes others, a brawler.
The message that agrees with the teaching he received from the apostles.
Readable explains the title (m1).

records.source: Εἰσὶν γὰρ πολλοὶ καὶ ἀνυπότακτοι, ματαιολόγοι καὶ φρεναπάται, μάλιστα οἱ ἐκ τῆς περιτομῆς, οὓς δεῖ ἐπιστομίζειν, οἵτινες ὅλους οἴκους ἀνατρέπουσιν διδάσκοντες ἃ μὴ δεῖ αἰσχροῦ κέρδους χάριν.
records.gloss: There are for many [and] insubordinate, empty talkers and deceivers, especially those of the circumcision, \v 11 whom it is necessary to silence, who whole households overturn, teaching what not they ought, of shameful gain for the sake.
pieces: For there are many rebellious people, full of empty talk and deception, especially those of the circumcision group.
They must be silenced, because they are ruining whole households by teaching what they should not, and doing it for dishonest gain.

L.10: For there are many who are insubordinate, empty talkers and deceivers, especially those of the circumcision [party],
L.11: who must be silenced, since they are upsetting whole households, teaching what they ought not, for the sake of shameful gain.

R.10: There are many people who will not obey. They talk about things that are worthless, and they fool people. Many of them are Jewish believers who say that people must be circumcised.
R.11: You must stop them from talking, because they are ruining whole families. They teach things they should not teach, and they do it to get money.

decisions.choice: those of the circumcision: Jewish believers who required circumcision
decisions.reason: Probably Jewish Christians who insisted on circumcision and the law (Galatians 2:12; Acts 11:2), as the "Jewish myths" of verse 14 suggest.
ἐπιστομίζειν is to stop the mouth, as with a muzzle or bridle.
Churches met in homes, so whole families and house churches were led astray (2 Timothy 3:6).

decisions.choice: Jewish believers who say that people must be circumcised
decisions.reason: Readable states the sense chosen in m1.

records.source: εἶπέν τις ἐξ αὐτῶν, ἴδιος αὐτῶν προφήτης, Κρῆτες ἀεὶ ψεῦσται, κακὰ θηρία, γαστέρες ἀργαί·
records.gloss: Said one of them, their own prophet: Cretans [are] always liars, evil beasts, idle bellies.
pieces: One of their own prophets has said, "Cretans are always liars, evil brutes, lazy gluttons."

L.12: One of them, their own prophet, said, "Cretans [are] always liars, evil beasts, lazy gluttons."

R.12: One of their own people, who they say was a prophet, said this: "People from Crete always lie. They are like wild animals. They are lazy and only want to eat."

decisions.choice: "Cretans are always liars": a Cretan poet
decisions.reason: The line is attributed to Epimenides of Crete (sixth century BC), whom Cretans honored as a seer. "To Cretanize" was Greek slang for "to lie".
γαστέρες ἀργαί is literally "lazy bellies": people ruled by appetite.
Paul uses the Cretans' own word for the poet; it does not mean he was a prophet of God.

decisions.choice: who they say was a prophet
decisions.reason: Readable makes m3 explicit.

R.13: And what he said is true.

decisions.reason: μαρτυρία is a witness or statement. Paul agrees with the description as it fits the false teachers, not as a judgment on every Cretan.

records.source: δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν ἔλεγχε αὐτοὺς ἀποτόμως, ἵνα ὑγιαίνωσιν ἐν τῇ πίστει, μὴ προσέχοντες Ἰουδαϊκοῖς μύθοις καὶ ἐντολαῖς ἀνθρώπων ἀποστρεφομένων τὴν ἀλήθειαν.
records.gloss: For which reason rebuke them sharply, so that they may be sound in the faith, \v 14 not paying attention to Jewish myths and commands of men turning away from the truth.
pieces: So rebuke them sharply, so that they may be sound in the faith
and pay no attention to Jewish myths or to the commands of people who reject the truth.

L.13: For this reason rebuke them sharply, so that they may be sound in the faith,
L.14: not paying attention to Jewish myths and commands of {{gender:people|men}} who turn away from the truth.

R.13: So you must warn them strongly, so that their faith will be healthy and true.
R.14: Then they will stop listening to Jewish stories that people have made up. They will stop obeying the rules of people who have turned away from the truth.

decisions.reason: ἀποτόμως is "cuttingly". The aim is restoration: that they may be sound.
Probably speculative stories built on the Old Testament and rules about clean and unclean things (verse 15; 1 Timothy 4:3; Colossians 2:20-22).
ἀνθρώπων is the general word for human beings.
The word means human beings in general (m3).

records.source: πάντα καθαρὰ τοῖς καθαροῖς· τοῖς δὲ μεμιαμμένοις καὶ ἀπίστοις οὐδὲν καθαρόν, ἀλλὰ μεμίανται αὐτῶν καὶ ὁ νοῦς καὶ ἡ συνείδησις.
records.gloss: All things [are] pure to the pure; to those but defiled and unbelieving nothing [is] pure, but are defiled their both mind and conscience.
pieces: To the pure, all things are pure, but to those who are corrupted and do not believe, nothing is pure. In fact, both their minds and their consciences are corrupted.

L.15: To the pure all things [are] pure, but to the defiled and unbelieving nothing [is] pure; but both their mind and their conscience are defiled.

R.15: To people who are pure in heart, everything is pure. But for people who have wrong desires and who do not believe, nothing is pure. Their minds and their sense of right and wrong are spoiled.

decisions.choice: to the pure all things are pure
decisions.reason: Against rules about ritual purity: what is unclean is the heart, not foods or things (Mark 7:15, 7:19; Romans 14:20).
μιαίνω is to stain or pollute; the false teachers worry about outward defilement but are defiled within.

records.source: θεὸν ὁμολογοῦσιν εἰδέναι, τοῖς δὲ ἔργοις ἀρνοῦνται, βδελυκτοὶ ὄντες καὶ ἀπειθεῖς καὶ πρὸς πᾶν ἔργον ἀγαθὸν ἀδόκιμοι.
records.gloss: God they profess to know, by the but works they deny [him], detestable being and disobedient and for every work good unfit.
pieces: They claim to know God, but by what they do they deny {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They are detestable and disobedient, and unfit for doing anything good.

L.16: They profess to know God, but they deny {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by their works. They are detestable and disobedient, unfit for any good work.

R.16: They say that they know God, but the things they do show that they do not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They are disgusting. They do not obey God, and they are not able to do anything good.

decisions.reason: ἀδόκιμοι is the opposite of "approved": tested and rejected (2 Timothy 3:8).

decisions.choice: deny him: the object is supplied
decisions.reason: ἀρνοῦνται has no object; "him", meaning God, is understood from the first clause.
The object is understood (m2).
